text: Which retina-specific GPCRs are specific to rod or cone photoreceptor cells (single-cell), have no detectable mRNA in liver, none in kidney and none in lung, and are not targets of FDA-approved drugs?
plan: Protein class: G-protein coupled receptors AND Tissue category (RNA): Retina / Tissue enriched AND Cell type category (scRNA): Cone photoreceptor cells, Rod photoreceptor cells / Cell type enriched AND NOT Protein class: FDA approved drug targets
understanding: Identify genes that are GPCRs, specific to retina, specific to rod or cone photoreceptors at the single-cell RNA level, lack detectable mRNA expression across liver, kidney, and lung, and are not targets of FDA-approved drugs.

trail.requirement: GPCRs (have no detectable mRNA in liver, none in kidney and none in lung)
trail.why: Selecting 'G-protein coupled receptors' at Level 1 restricts the query to all GPCRs without narrowing to a specific subclass.

To identify retina-specific genes, the retina tissue must be selected with the 'Tissue enriched' category, defined as having at least four-fold higher mRNA expression in that tissue compared to any other tissue.

trail.requirement: specific to rod or cone photoreceptor cells (single-cell)
trail.why: The question specifically asks for genes that are specific to rod or cone photoreceptor cells in single-cell data, which corresponds to the 'Cell type enriched' specificity category in those cell types.
Selecting the class 'FDA approved drug targets' without restricting the subclass captures all targets of FDA-approved drugs to be excluded by the requirement.

requirements.requirement: GPCRs (have no detectable mRNA in liver, none in kidney and none in lung)
requirements.why: G-protein coupled receptors constitute a well-defined functional subclass within the 'Protein class' field.
'Tissue category (RNA)' defines tissue-specific RNA expression profiles across human tissues, including retina.

requirements.requirement: specific to rod or cone photoreceptor cells (single-cell)
requirements.why: This field evaluates RNA specificity and distribution across single-cell types, which directly includes rod and cone photoreceptor cells.
The question explicitly excludes targets of FDA-approved drugs, which is a defined option ('FDA approved drug targets') under 'Protein class'.
